title: Admit athena.toml changes by the candidate's own Config schema
summary: Admission parses a changed athena.toml with the running Athena's compiled `Config`, so a job that adds a section and its schema field together is always refused (jobs q0xy and qcrz hit this on `[parallel]`). Change admission so the candidate's config is checked against the candidate's own schema, while a config with a genuinely unknown field is still refused. The audience is Athena's operator and future jobs that extend the config.

defaults_applied.how: New admission tests cover the admitted, still-refused, and fail-closed cases; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Fix the rule that checks the config against the wrong schema, not just the `[parallel]` instance.
Criteria run admission on a config-plus-schema change and check the outcome.
A criterion reproduces the exact failure of the two named jobs.
The fail-closed criterion prevents an unrunnable candidate check from counting as a pass.
The change is Rust in athena-core.
One focused change in admission.rs; defaults.toml handled only if it falls out of the same mechanism.
The rule is enforced by admission tests, not prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Read from crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs lines 215-238: the 'configuration' rule calls Config::parse (the base binary's athena_data::Config, which uses deny_unknown_fields in config.rs) on the candidate's athena.toml.

Candidate commit C is a tree in the user's git repo, not built before admission (run.rs ~846), so the candidate's schema must be exercised by checking out/building the candidate's athena-data crate, e.g. in a temporary tree, and running a small check against it.
Where the candidate does not change the schema (crates/athena-data/src/config.rs), behavior stays as today: parse with the running Config.

The candidate's schema check must fail closed: if the candidate's own check cannot be built or run, or reports an error, admission yields a 'configuration' violation with the real message, never silent success.
defaults.toml (DefaultsModel) has the same shape of problem; fix it the same way only if it falls out of the same mechanism, otherwise leave it.
Landing still re-parses the config with the base Config where it does today; if landing has the same flaw it is noted rather than silently left. Check crates/athena-gate/src/lib.rs line 140 for that.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new admission test shows a candidate that adds a new `[section]` to athena.toml together with the matching field in athena-data's Config is admitted with no 'configuration' violation. Run `cargo test -p athena-core admission`.

A new admission test shows a candidate that adds an unknown `[section]` to athena.toml without changing the schema is still refused with a 'configuration' violation naming the unknown field. Run `cargo test -p athena-core admission`.
A test shows that when the candidate's own schema check cannot run or fails, admission reports a 'configuration' violation instead of passing. Run `cargo test -p athena-core admission`.
admission.rs documents (module comment and rule comment) that a changed athena.toml is judged by the candidate's schema, and states how the candidate's schema is obtained.
The existing admission tests (bad athena.toml, defaults.toml, docs/athena.toml) still pass; `cargo test` passes and `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

Outcome check: the failure text from jobs 20261016-071202-q0xy and 20261016-185517-qcrz (`unknown field parallel` when athena.toml and the schema change together) is reproduced by a test and no longer occurs.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the admission change, if the repository's CHANGELOG convention covers behavior changes.

out_of_scope: Building parallel jobs themselves (job q0xy's request) and the [parallel] config section.
departures: Slightly lower pass odds and higher cost than the reference: the fix needs the candidate's schema built and exercised from admission, which is a design choice with fail-closed edge cases.
